record.paper_title: Current work and open problems in the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
record.original_question: Consider the neutral Volterra functional integro-differential equation u'(t) = a(t)u(t) + b(t)u(θ(t)) + c(t)u'(θ(t)) + \int_0^t [K_{0,0}(t,s)u(s) + K_{0,1}(t,s)u'(s)]ds + \int_0^{θ(t)} [K_{1,0}(t,s)u(s) + K_{1,1}(t,s)u'(s)]ds on a uniform mesh, with θ(t) = qt and 0 < q < 1. If u_h \in S^{(0)}_m(I_h) is the collocation solution at Gauss points, is the optimal pointwise superconvergence order p* equal to 2m for m = 1,2 and m + 2 for m > 2, and can one also choose collocation parameters so that the same estimate holds for u'_h?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3.1 Suppose that uh \in S(0) m (Ih) is the collocation solution to the initial-value problem for the neutral VFIDE (3.1) with respect to the Gauss points {ci} in (2.2) with θ(t) = qt (0 <q< 1). Prove that for sufficiently smooth data, the optimal order of superconvergence of uh at the points of a uniform mesh Ih, max t\inIh |u(t) − uh(t)| \le Cm(q)hp* , is given by p* = { 2m, m = 1, 2, m + 2, m> 2. Are there collocation parameters {ci} so that the above estimate is also true for u' h?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $0<q<1$ and let $\theta(t)=qt$. Consider the neutral Volterra functional integro-differential equation
$$u'(t)=a(t)u(t)+b(t)u(\theta(t))+c(t)u'(\theta(t))+\int_0^t\!\big[K_{0,0}(t,s)u(s)+K_{0,1}(t,s)u'(s)\big]ds+\int_0^{\theta(t)}\!\big[K_{1,0}(t,s)u(s)+K_{1,1}(t,s)u'(s)\big]ds,\qquad t\in I:=[0,T],$$
together with the initial condition $u(0)=u_0$, where the coefficients $a,b,c$ and the kernels $K_{i,j}$ ($i,j\in\{0,1\}$) are sufficiently smooth on $I$ and on $\{(t,s):0\le s\le t\le T\}$ respectively.

Let $I_h=\{t_n=nh:0\le n\le N,\;Nh=T\}$ be a uniform mesh on $I$ and set $\sigma_n=(t_n,t_{n+1}]$. For an integer $m\ge1$ and collocation parameters $0<c_1<\cdots<c_m\le 1$, the collocation space is
$$S_m^{(0)}(I_h)=\{v\in C(I):v|_{\sigma_n}\in\pi_m,\ 0\le n\le N-1\},$$
where $\pi_m$ denotes polynomials of degree at most $m$. Let $u_h\in S_m^{(0)}(I_h)$ be the collocation solution determined by requiring that $u_h$ satisfies the equation above (with $u$ replaced by $u_h$) at the collocation points $t_{n,i}:=t_n+c_i h$, and that $u_h(0)=u_0$. Choose the $\{c_i\}$ as the $m$ Gauss points (zeros of the shifted Legendre polynomial of degree $m$ on $[0,1]$).

Define the optimal order of pointwise superconvergence on $I_h$ as the largest $p^*$ such that
$$\max_{t\in I_h}|u(t)-u_h(t)|\le C_m(q)\,h^{p^*}$$
holds for all sufficiently smooth data, with $C_m(q)$ independent of $h$.

(a) Prove or disprove that
$$p^*=\begin{cases}2m,&m=1,2,\\ m+2,&m>2.\end{cases}$$
(b) Determine whether there exist choices of collocation parameters $\{c_i\}$ such that the same estimate is valid with $u(t)-u_h(t)$ replaced by $u'(t)-u'_h(t)$ at the points of $I_h$.
artifact.category_tag: collocation methods for delay Volterra integro-differential equations
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (notably on optimal superconvergence for Volterra functional integral equations with proportional vanishing delays, 2017) resolved related conjectures for non-neutral VFIEs on quasi-geometric/uniform meshes, showing local superconvergence at mesh points cannot exceed m+2. However, no source explicitly verifying the conjectured orders (2m for m=1,2 and m+2 for m>2) for the neutral VFIDE on a uniform mesh, nor the analogous estimate for the derivative u'_h, was found. The status for the neutral case appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Optimal superconvergence results for Volterra functional integral equations with proportional vanishing delays
status_evidence.snippet: On uniform meshes, the iterated collocation solution possesses global superconvergence order m+1, and the order of local superconvergence at the nodes cannot exceed m+2.
status_evidence.claim: Related (non-neutral) case partially resolved; bound m+2 confirmed on uniform meshes.

status_evidence.title: Superconvergence in Collocation Methods on Quasi-Graded Meshes for Functional Differential Equations with Vanishing Delays
status_evidence.snippet: Collocation methods on quasi-graded meshes for functional differential equations with vanishing delays.
status_evidence.claim: Related superconvergence analyses exist, but not specifically for the neutral VFIDE problem stated.
